display_name: Talk tables ПТ-1 and ПТ-2 (переговорные таблицы)
status: Placeholder tables for simcore/talk_tables.hpp: the regiment's voice orders on its command net (FuG-3, R-111) go out as three-digit groups of ПТ-1; the battery's signals (warnings) as groups of ПТ-2. Read by the crew (an NPC decodes, a player reads the document on his desk). docs/crew/12_COMMUNICATIONS.md §2.9.
notes: That troop air defence kept talk tables (переговорные таблицы, таблицы сигналов), coded maps and call-sign tables is documented (pvo_bu_x_1984); that «ПТ-<n>» names a talk table is attested (fsrbit_pt). The 1980s tables themselves were controlled documents and were not sought. The form is that of post-Soviet samples: tactical terms as three-digit groups (bstudy_tactics, an AA missile regiment's table of 1999, readiness no. 1 = 143), a signal table with a radio code and a spoken word per signal (bstudy_tactics: 333 «Воздух», 777 «Отбой»; sfu_tactics_2011 has 555 for the air alarm: the samples disagree, and every group here is SAM3D's). Air data, target designations and warnings may be said in clear (pvo_bu_x_1984 art. 30): the tables cover orders and signals, not targets. `aspd` ties an entry to the ASPD-U's two-digit command of the same meaning (data/command/aspd_codes.json), so a regiment's order sent both ways means one thing.
source: bstudy_tactics (the form: three-digit groups, readiness no. 1 = 143, signals 333 «Воздух» and 777 «Отбой»); fsrbit_pt (ПТ-<n> = переговорная таблица); pvo_bu_x_1984 (art. 30: what may be said in clear); the groups are a sam3d placeholder
